partners.mechanism_chain: VIM (HGNC:12003) —DISRUPTS→ Impaired Lens Crystallin Expression/Assembly (HP:0030171); Impaired Lens Crystallin Expression/Assembly (HP:0030171) —LEADS_TO→ Cataract (HP:0000119); IL2RG (HGNC:5543) —DISRUPTS→ Cytokine Signaling Pathway (GO:0007169); Cytokine Signaling Pathway (GO:0007169) —DECREASES→ Lymphocyte Development and Function (HP:0002715); Lymphocyte Development and Function (HP:0002715) —LEADS_TO→ T-B+ severe combined immunodeficiency (HP:0001861); VIM (HGNC:12003) —BINDS→ Cytokine Signaling Pathway (GO:0007169); Cytokine Signaling Pathway (GO:0007169) —DECREASES→ Cataract (HP:0000119). Mutations in VIM (Vimentin) disrupt lens fiber cell structure and crystallin expression, leading to cataract. Vimentin also interacts with components of the cytokine signaling pathway, including IL2RG. Mutations in IL2RG disrupt the common gamma chain's function in cytokine signaling, impairing lymphocyte development and function, leading to T-B+ SCID. The overlap occurs because Vimentin's role extends to modulating cellular signaling pathways that are also critically dependent on IL2RG function.

#### 1. T-B+ severe combined immunodeficiency due to gamma chain deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.396)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6785807)

**Proposed mechanism:** VIM (HGNC:12003) —DISRUPTS→ Impaired Lens Crystallin Expression/Assembly (HP:0030171); Impaired Lens Crystallin Expression/Assembly (HP:0030171) —LEADS_TO→ Cataract (HP:0000119); IL2RG (HGNC:5543) —DISRUPTS→ Cytokine Signaling Pathway (GO:0007169); Cytokine Signaling Pathway (GO:0007169) —DECREASES→ Lymphocyte Development and Function (HP:0002715); Lymphocyte Development and Function (HP:0002715) —LEADS_TO→ T-B+ severe combined immunodeficiency (HP:0001861); VIM (HGNC:12003) —BINDS→ Cytokine Signaling Pathway (GO:0007169); Cytokine Signaling Pathway (GO:0007169) —DECREASES→ Cataract (HP:0000119). Mutations in VIM (Vimentin) disrupt lens fiber cell structure and crystallin expression, leading to cataract. Vimentin also interacts with components of the cytokine signaling pathway, including IL2RG. Mutations in IL2RG disrupt the common gamma chain's function in cytokine signaling, impairing lymphocyte development and function, leading to T-B+ SCID. The overlap occurs because Vimentin's role extends to modulating cellular signaling pathways that are also critically dependent on IL2RG function.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of interaction or co-localization between Vimentin and components of the IL2RG-mediated cytokine signaling pathway in relevant cell types (e.g., lens epithelial cells, lymphocytes) would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if genetic studies reveal no variants in VIM associated with any form of cataract, or no variants in IL2RG associated with any form of SCID, this would also challenge the proposed link.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the mechanistic link between VIM and IL2RG could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both cataract and severe combined immunodeficiency. Modulating Vimentin's interaction with cytokine signaling pathways might offer a strategy to mitigate immune dysfunction in SCID patients, or conversely, targeting IL2RG-related signaling could potentially impact VIM-dependent cellular processes in the lens, offering new avenues for cataract treatment.
